subject: history
topicDisplay: The Peoples Health C1250 To Present
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: X-rays, used to locate bullets and shrapnel in WWI, had been discovered by Wilhelm Rontgen in which year?
questions.explain: Rontgen discovered X-rays in 1895, and mobile units were used near the WWI front.

questions.q: Florence Nightingale is best known for transforming which aspect of medicine after the Crimean War?
options: Hospital hygiene and the training of nurses
questions.explain: Nightingale improved hospital cleanliness and founded modern nursing training in 1860.

questions.q: Which medical service was responsible for evacuating and treating wounded soldiers on the WWI Western Front?
questions.explain: The Royal Army Medical Corps ran the chain of evacuation from the front line to base hospitals.

questions.q: On the WWI Western Front, the Thomas splint was used to treat which type of injury?
questions.explain: The Thomas splint immobilised broken legs and dramatically reduced deaths from femur fractures.

questions.q: Why did the work of Vesalius, Pare and Harvey have only limited impact on everyday treatment at the time?
options: Most doctors still followed Galen and few practical cures resulted at first
Their ideas spread instantly and cured most diseases
questions.explain: Their discoveries advanced knowledge but did not immediately change how ordinary patients were treated.

questions.q: Joseph Lister introduced which substance as an antiseptic during surgery?
questions.explain: Lister used carbolic acid to kill germs during operations, greatly reducing post-surgical infection.

questions.q: The National Health Service (NHS) was established in Britain in which year?
questions.explain: The NHS launched in 1948, providing healthcare free at the point of use, led by Aneurin Bevan.

questions.q: The French surgeon Ambroise Pare improved the treatment of gunshot wounds in the 16th century by replacing hot oil with what?
options: A soothing ointment of egg yolk, rose oil and turpentine
questions.explain: Pare found a gentle salve healed wounds better than cauterising them with boiling oil.

questions.q: Penicillin was first mass-produced and used widely to treat soldiers during which event?
questions.explain: Florey and Chain developed mass production so penicillin could treat wounded WWII soldiers.

questions.q: In 1796 Edward Jenner developed a vaccination against which disease?
questions.explain: Jenner showed in 1796 that cowpox could protect people against smallpox, creating the first vaccine.

questions.q: Andreas Vesalius is best remembered in the history of medicine for his work on which area?
questions.explain: Vesalius produced detailed, accurate anatomical drawings and corrected several of Galen's errors.

questions.q: According to Galen, an excess of phlegm could be balanced by giving the patient a remedy with which opposite quality?
questions.explain: Galen's theory of opposites treated cold, wet phlegm with hot, dry remedies such as pepper.

questions.q: During the Black Death of 1348, many people believed the plague was a punishment sent by whom?
questions.explain: Most medieval people saw the Black Death as God's punishment for human sin.

questions.q: In 1854 Dr John Snow famously traced a cholera outbreak to which source?
options: A contaminated water pump in Broad Street
Bad air rising from the Thames
questions.explain: Snow linked the Soho cholera outbreak to the Broad Street water pump, evidence that cholera spread through water.

questions.q: In medieval Britain, ill health was widely explained by an imbalance in which four substances?
options: The four humours: blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile
The four winds described by Hippocrates
The four miasmas of the body
The four elements of earth, air, fire and water
questions.explain: Medieval medicine relied on the Theory of the Four Humours, inherited from the Ancient Greeks.

questions.q: On the WWI Western Front, the use of stored blood for transfusion was made possible by adding what to stop clotting?
questions.explain: Adding sodium citrate let blood be stored, allowing transfusions to save wounded soldiers.

questions.q: The Germ Theory of disease was developed in the 1860s chiefly by which scientist?
questions.explain: Louis Pasteur published his Germ Theory in 1861, showing microbes rather than miasma caused decay and disease.

questions.q: William Harvey is famous for proving which idea in the 17th century?
options: That germs in the air cause disease
That blood is continuously made in the liver and consumed
That the body contains four humours
That the heart pumps and circulates the blood around the body
questions.explain: Harvey demonstrated that the heart acts as a pump circulating blood, overturning Galen's view.

questions.q: In what year did the Black Death first reach Britain?
questions.explain: The Black Death arrived in England in 1348, killing roughly a third to half the population.

questions.q: The first effective anaesthetic widely used in surgery, chloroform, was demonstrated by James Simpson in which decade?
questions.explain: James Simpson introduced chloroform as a surgical anaesthetic in 1847.

questions.q: The structure of DNA as a double helix was identified by Crick and Watson in which year?
questions.explain: Crick and Watson published the double-helix structure of DNA in 1953.

questions.q: Alexander Fleming is credited with the 1928 discovery of which substance?
questions.explain: Fleming noticed that penicillin mould killed bacteria, the first true antibiotic, though others later developed it.
